case_name: Sri. Vijjagir Sureshchander S/O. Sri ... vs The State Of Telangana

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Sri. Vijjagir Sureshchander S/O. Sri ... (husband, wife, plaintiff)
parties.respondent_defendant: The State Of Telangana (wife, husband, defendant)

acts_cited_auto: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

acts_cited.act: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

facts_of_case: Petitioners were married in 2012. Respondent filed complaint against petitioners under Sections 498-A, 506 of IPC. Petitioners claim FIR No.78/2015 is illegal and arbitrary.

legal_principles.principle: Abuse of process of law can be quashed.
legal_principles.held: He relies on the decision in Smt.Yamunabai Anantrao Adhav v. Anantrao Shivram Adhav 1.
cited_cases: Smt.Yamunabai Anantrao Adhav v. Anantrao Shivram Adhav, (Year) X SCC Y

legal_principles.principle: The court's jurisdiction under Article 226 should not be exercised to quash a FIR/DVC without verifying the authenticity of documents.
legal_principles.held: This Court in exercise of its jurisdiction under Article 226 first take up the issue whether the documents i.e. voter I.D. card, declaration certificate etc. relied on by the petitioners are true or forged and thereafter record a finding whether grounds are made out for quashing the FIR/DVC.

outcome.final_order: Writ petitions disposed of by common order; FIR No.78/2015 quashed as illegal, arbitrary, and in violation of provisions of Hindu Marriage Act, Constitution of India.
